project_specification.project_name: nullius — feature 282 (System computes leave-one-family-out transfer by holding an entire theme root out of the pool, which returns the delta on that held-out theme)
project_specification.addition_summary: Implement app_spec.xml feature 282 in the existing dreaming member (packages/dreaming, import name dreaming; seat src/app/modules/dreaming): the family-shaped holdout §4.5 calls a standing requirement — "Hold an entire theme root out of the dreaming pool, then evaluate on worlds from that theme. It measures transfer directly, costs almost nothing, and is the only honest way to tell learned research discipline from memorized family texture." docs/alpha-engine-prd.md §11 carries the metric ("ΔIR on a held-out theme root", target "> 0"), §12's M3 exit repeats the bar, §13 names it the mitigation for a family-specific overfit signature, and §15 is why the holdout must be family-shaped rather than world-shaped: "shape features do not [transfer] and two of them invert sign across families." docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md §11.1 spells the call in code — "# Standing metric: hold an entire theme out of the dreaming pool, evaluate on it. lofo_delta_ir = evaluate(policy, worlds_of_theme(held_out_theme))" — and §16 lists the metric among the research metrics. One new module, dreaming/transfer.py, three spellings of one act. (1) The judgment — leave_one_family_out(themes, *, theme, floor=LADDER_FLOOR_WORLDS): the pool's families (a mapping of world id to the theme root that world belongs to) and the root to hold out in, a FamilyPartition out, the shape of the ladder's other verdicts (rejects_thin_pool, revision_cap, split_pool) — a pure function of what the caller already holds, never opening a database. The holdout is ENTIRE by construction: every world whose root is the named theme is held out, everything else retained, decided by nothing but the root — there is no parameter that could hold half a family out. Both halves in the pool's id order (the same total order pool_worlds answers), so the same census constructs the same partition in any process; roots (every family the pool carried) and family_count/world_count carried so an operator sees the pool's breadth; is_held_out/is_retained predicates for the caller marking readings, both REFUSING a world the partition does not hold rather than answering False (a world outside the pool is in no family, and an answer that read as one side would let a caller mark a world the holdout never saw). The floor judges the pool that REMAINS, delegated to feature 275's rejects_thin_pool over the retained count in the floor's own word — a transfer figure over a selection that could never have run is a number about nothing — so a pool whose worlds all carry one root (the campaign-diversity failure) is refused by the delegated floor as an empty retained half, not by a second law minted here. (2) The call — family_transfer(candidate, baseline, *, themes, theme, floor, spread, delta, power): §11.1's line made to run. Both arms' per-world out-of-sample IR readings are restricted to the worlds of the held-out root ONLY, and the differences over exactly those worlds are tested paired through feature 281's paired_ir_difference — the arithmetic is consumed, never respelled, because the delta on a held-out theme IS a paired comparison over that theme's worlds. Readings for any other world are not evaluated: that is the hold-out itself rather than a drop, and it is what makes the figure a transfer measurement — nothing the selection could have read on the held-out family is in the comparison (the reason the 70/30 split of feature 278 cannot replace this holdout: a random 30% carries every family nearly in proportion, so the holdout worlds of family F sat beside train worlds of F in the pool the selection read, and memorised family texture passes it). Everything downstream of the restriction is delegated to the pairing's own law in its own vocabulary (PairedComparisonError): a family world only one arm carries, a family too small to spread, a non-finite figure, the capacity keywords passed straight through so the two spellings of §11.0's arithmetic cannot disagree. Returns a FamilyTransfer carrying the held-out root, its worlds (the evidence the delta is over), the retained count (the pool the selection runs over, the figure the delegated floor judged), and feature 281's PairedDifference whole — carried rather than flattened, with delta_ir (§11.1's own variable name) and transfers (§11's "> 0", strict: a delta of exactly zero is not transfer) as the record's readings of it. (3) The family is the caller's fact — theme_root is not a column of the pool's tables and this module does not invent one; the family a world belongs to is carried by the question seam's meta() (architecture §11) and the adapters that wrap each pool's worlds, and no member imports another, so the caller hands the census in whole as a mapping of world id to theme root, the same stance split_pool takes for the pool's ids. The seam validates what it reads: non-empty text ids and roots, a bare string REFUSED where a mapping belongs (Python would iterate its characters as worlds — a pool nobody holds, divided into families nobody authored), a root the pool does not carry refused naming the roots it does carry (a root with no worlds removes nothing, and an empty holdout's refusal would describe a pairing failure where the fact is a stale census). (4) The store seam — pooled_family_transfer(candidate_policy, baseline_policy, *, themes, theme, database_url, floor, spread, delta, power, env): the two arms named by policy_version, the database resolved the way the split's and the comparison's seams resolve it (an explicit URL first, then DATABASE_URL, refused by name when neither names one, and feature 270's FreezeRequestError from the URL seam TRANSLATED into this module's class), the pool's membership read through feature 278's pool_worlds (the union law — a world once, whichever half names it), each arm's readings read through feature 281's _pool_arm (last row by id, deterministically), and the transfer answered over them. The families must cover the pool EXACTLY, in both directions: a census that misses pool worlds leaves them in no family — invisible to a partition claiming to be of the pool, silently free to sit under a selection that believed their family was gone — and a census naming worlds the store does not hold grounds the figure on worlds that do not exist; both refused with the disagreement named, because "holding an entire theme root out of the pool" is a claim about the pool and at the store seam the pool is ground truth. One policy named as both arms is refused before any database is opened (every difference exactly zero — a figure reporting no transfer while looking like a measurement of it). The transfer WRITES NOTHING: it is a read, so it runs under feature 270's hold, which is load-bearing — §C5 holds the pool fixed for the whole outer iteration and the standing metric is what the iteration computes during it. Two new error SIBLINGS under DreamingError, split by the REPAIR the caller must make: TransferRequestError for the ask's own facts and TransferStoreError for a store that holds no pool or no honest census of one. No code word: feature 282's verb is "computes", so every refusal opens with its subject (the shape features 276/278's classes state); neither class ever mints feature 275's pool_too_thin or feature 281's codes, both delegated where they apply. No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings, or migration is edited; no table is created or written; no new @register component is added (feature 270's single "dreaming" component is untouched); the member joins by workspace-scan convention and does not import another workspace member (the membership law and the arm read are consumed from the member's own siblings). The module is stdlib-only: os, collections.abc, pathlib, typing.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace (packages/* members, import names are underscored slugs) / pytest (ruff + mypy conventions). The module loader (src/app/module_loader.py) discovers members from the root pyproject.toml `[tool.uv.workspace] members = ["packages/*"]`, imports each package so its module-level `@register` fires, and composes what each `@register` builder contributes under a component name. `app` (src/app) is a namespace package with no `__init__.py`; the seats in src/app/modules/ <member>/ are reached by namespace import (e.g. app.modules.dreaming). A member never imports another member — it reaches shared shapes through `app.*`, never through a sibling package's import name.
existing_context.test_baseline: The repository-level suite under tests/ is collected by pytest with testpaths=tests; each workspace member's own suite lives under packages/<member>/tests/ and is collected under its own conftest (same-basename files collide under one pytest run), and is NOT graded by the bare `uv run pytest` acceptance gate — a member suite must be run explicitly (run both `uv run pytest tests/` and the member's own `packages/dreaming/tests/`). Baseline before this feature: 365 passed in packages/dreaming/tests, 1084 passed at the repository level. The repo lint is red on main (mypy absent, pre-existing ruff errors), so lint only the changed files and compare to a sibling. The dreaming member is stdlib-only, and feature 282 keeps it that way: os, collections.abc, pathlib, typing.
existing_context.conventions: snake_case modules, hand-written __slots__ value classes for records (this member's FreezeRecord/PoolSplit/CapRecord/PairedDifference precedent), docstrings that cite the governing documents by section and quote the sentence they implement, refusals that name the subject and the repair, error classes split by the repair rather than by where the failure was noticed, and delegation rather than restatement wherever a sibling already owns the law (the floor to ladder.rejects_thin_pool, the membership to split.pool_worlds, the arithmetic and the pairing to paired.paired_ir_difference). The member's honesty stance: a module cites the document it implements and says what it is NOT (this one is not the selector, not the 70/30 split, not the bar, not the campaign constraint; it is no component, holds nothing, writes nothing).
existing_context.context: existing modules in packages/dreaming/src/dreaming/: errors.py (the member's vocabulary), layout.py (the pool's restated shape), cycle.py (feature 270's freeze, and sqlite_path), ladder.py (feature 275, the floor), ceiling.py (feature 276), cap.py (feature 277), split.py (feature 278, the 70/30 train/holdout split whose pool_worlds this feature's store seam consumes), paired.py (feature 281, the paired continuous statistic this feature's delta IS, restricted to a family). Tests live in packages/dreaming/tests/ with their own conftest.py providing database_url, pool, scores and freeze fixtures.

deliverables.deliverable: packages/dreaming/src/dreaming/transfer.py — the judgment, the call and the store seam, with leave_one_family_out, family_transfer, pooled_family_transfer, FamilyPartition and FamilyTransfer in __all__. No @register, no table, no write, no new constants (the floor and the power are consumed from their owning modules).

packages/dreaming/tests/test_transfer.py — the feature's own suite: the holdout pinned entire (every world of the family, only those, in id order whatever the census order), the floor judging the retained pool in the ladder's own word, the delta agreeing with an independently restricted paired comparison and not moving when retained readings move, the unknown root refused naming the carried ones, the census shape, the delegated pairing laws, and the store seam (writes nothing, runs under a hold, the exact-cover census in both directions, the union law over the scores fixture); test_errors.py extended with the sibling pin against the member's whole vocabulary; test_cross_member.py extended with the read pinned against a pool built by 0109's own apply() and feature 188's own store.
